findings.where: Air sheet Note 1, with screen 12 (Isolate the receiver), its why and the State tab line
findings.what: Note 1 says V7 is opened only while R1 is out of service, but screen 12 says to keep V7 shut while R1 is out for inspection. The sheet cannot do what Note 1 says anyway: R1 has no inlet valve of its own, because the joined compressor line tees straight into R1 and up to V7. So with V1, V2 and V3 shut the compressors are cut off, and V7 could only join R1 to the header. Either give R1 its own inlet valve between the tee and R1 (screen 12's answer then becomes that valve and V3, and V7 may open), or rewrite Note 1 so it no longer names R1 out of service.

findings.where: Screen 13 (The starter still live): task, why and the after-Check motion
findings.what: Nothing explains how -Q23 came to be closed. The sheet draws it N.O., and the interlock only allows it to close. Yet after Check it swings shut on its own 0.8 s after -Q13 is locked off, which suggests an automatic changeover the sheet never shows. Say who closes it, for example 'Someone at the board then closes -Q23 to keep the pump running', or ask 'What else must you lock off before you start?'

findings.where: Screen 14 (Sheet and plant): why and the ink ring after Check
findings.what: 'So shutting V3 leaves the hose point live' says too little. V6 is open, so the untagged pipe keeps the whole header and all three users fed. The say line and the K.check both say this, but the why and the ring name only the hose point. Write 'With V3 shut, R1 still feeds the hose point, and back through V6 the whole header', ring all three users in the plant, and replace the unclear 'The extra pipe does.'

findings.where: Screen 2 Trace line, and every Trace, What if and description line on the air sheet and the plant
findings.what: pathWords, wrongWords and flowDesc give plural loads singular verbs: 'The tools gets air from C1 through NR1, V1, R1, V3 and V4', 'The tools still has air', 'The tools has no air'. Give the tools and the valve actuators a plural flag.

findings.where: Screen 6 (The state it is drawn in), the say line under the sheet
findings.what: With the State tab on, TABW.sb2.state and flowDesc both say 'Section 2 is fed from section 1 through bus-tie -Q8', and the screen's own text says it a third time. Drop the flowDesc sentence while the State tab is on.

It is one 33-word list sentence that also gives the bracket's scale and sizes, which nothing uses before screen 11. Trim it to 'Five practice sheets: an air system, two switchboards, a hoist's control schematic and a bracket drawing.'
In 'Its pressure falls as the users take air, then they stop.', 'they' could mean the compressors. Write 'Its pressure falls as the users take air. Then the users stop.'

findings.where: Screen 2 or 4, the What if button
findings.what: No screen invites him to use What if. The lesson's main idea, marking each load Runs or Stops, playing it and seeing misses ringed in red, is only found by stumbling on an unexplained button. Add one sentence, with its read, to a SHOW screen: 'Turn on What if, change one part, and mark each load before you play it.'

The choices name both differences, so the screen finds them for him, though the brief asked him to find where sheet and plant differ. Consider having him tap the difference that matters on the plant sketch, or describe the pipe less exactly.

findings.where: Screen 13 (The starter still live) right choice
findings.what: '-Q23, its second feed, from section B' gives its own reason. Shorten it to '-Q23, from section B'.

Four of the nine puzzles use the air sheet, and the hoist and the bracket get one each. No fluid-power circuit, such as a 4/3 or 5/2 valve with a cylinder, appears, though three lessons teach them and the brief asked for puzzles evenly from all four kinds. The brief's say-it-back, reporting the key features to a colleague, is also missing.

findings.where: Air sheet notes line during the Four steps demo (film s1)
findings.what: Note 1's amber highlight snaps on for Legend and State, and off for Sources and Trace, while the rings fade in. Give .notes a short background transition.
-G4 has no tap target and gives no message. Yet the explain says a stopped generator counts as a source because it can be started. A tap on it should at least say why it stays stopped here.
The '440 V' label runs into the -Q1 riser. Move it a few units left, or below the busbar.
